positioning.heading: Trek through a wilderness where no vehicle can ever go
positioning.body: Look at the landscape before you. Smell the wildflowers. Listen to the birds. Relax in a rock shelter under the Aboriginal paintings on the walls. Swim after swim in clear, tropical pools. Campsites you share with no one but your walking companions, because you walked to get there.

features.heading: Everything on your back, and no hurry
features.body: On every trip you carry a pack with your food and equipment. You need reasonable fitness, but these are not endurance tests. Trips run from three or four days to six week expeditions, some relatively easy, others relatively difficult, and all with plenty of time to stop for a swim, a three course meal by the campfire and the most amazing star show on earth.

features.heading: Guides who have walked this country for decades
features.body: Russell Willis helped found the Darwin Bushwalking Club in 1974 and started Willis's Walkabouts in 1986 with one man and one vehicle. Eleven guides carry Wilderness or Remote First Aid, and every major expedition carries a satellite phone and a backup EPIRB. No two trips are alike, and no other operator offers treks that leave the tracks behind for a week at a time.

offers.heading: Eight trips to start with
offers.intro: From accommodated day walks to a helicopter into the Bungle Bungles in the Wet. The full program of 47 departures is on the home page under All trips by date.

story.heading: One man, one vehicle, 1986
story.body:
Russell Willis came to Darwin in early 1974 and fell in love with the Top End bush. Within months he was helping found the Darwin Bushwalking Club, and as its first president he pioneered many of the routes local bushwalkers use today. Wishing to share that with a wider group of people, he started Willis's Walkabouts as a one man, one vehicle operation in Kakadu and the Kimberley in 1986. A year later there were two guides and two vehicles.

The business grew and new areas were added: the Pilbara, the Red Centre, and trips abroad. Darwin is still the base, closer to Jakarta and Singapore than to Sydney, and Cassie Newnes co manages the office and logistics with Russell between her own trips.

cta.heading: Book early and the discount is yours
cta.body: Book and pay four months ahead to save 20 percent, three months for 15, two months for 10. Trips need four or five bookings to run, and those who book late are often disappointed.

about.heading: About Willis's Walkabouts
about.intro: Based in Darwin on the north central coast of Australia, Willis's Walkabouts runs bushwalking holidays in four regions: the Top End, the Red Centre, the Kimberley and the Pilbara, with a few trips abroad each year.
about.story:
Bushwalking, trekking, hiking, backpacking, tramping: whatever you call these holidays, they are different. They begin where the four wheel drive tours stop. On every trip the guides lead you off the trail into places with Aboriginal rock art, gorges, birds, wildflowers, waterfalls and campsites you share with no one but your walking companions. They are yours alone because you walked to get there.

There are no phones, no cars, no people and no hassle: places where you swim in clear tropical pools, camp under the stars, enjoy a three course meal by the campfire and relax the evening away with a group of like minded people. Groups are four to twelve plus one or more guides, and every trip takes its time. Willis's Walkabouts is a Sustainable Tourism accredited business.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.intro: Email is best. If the office is slow to reply, it is because everyone is out doing what they love: bushwalking. Please be patient if we are out of range.

privateGroups.heading: Charter and group trips
privateGroups.intro: Get five or more people together for a group discount, or charter a trip that runs for your group alone.
privateGroups.body: Get five or more people together and apply for a group discount: 5 percent for five or more, 10 percent for ten or more. For a charter or personalised trip, tell the office where you want to walk, how long for and when, and Russell will put an itinerary together from forty years of routes. Some places can only be reached by chartered helicopter, float plane or boat, so charters are priced trip by trip.

gettingThere.meetingPoint: Trips leave from Darwin, Kununurra, Alice Springs or Tom Price, with pick up from your accommodation. Each trip page gives its own city and pre trip meeting.
gettingThere.notes: There is an important pre trip meeting the evening before departure. Trips normally leave about 8 am in the Northern Territory and earlier in Western Australia. Never schedule flights on the day a trip or section begins or ends without checking first.

seasons.note: The Wet: waterfalls and wildflowers, warm rain that is a pleasure to walk in. Every Kakadu, Top End and Kimberley trip from Christmas to March is a wet season trip.
The Dry: clear skies and weather so reliable that few people carry tents. Cool nights in the Centre and the Pilbara.
The Build Up: thunderstorms and the sudden greening of the land, the most dramatic season of all. Birds concentrate at the last waterholes.
